cards.name: Cervical part of internal carotid artery
cards.function: First part of the internal carotid, carrying blood from the carotid bifurcation to the skull base without giving any branch.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Carotid bifurcation at the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C4).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the carotid sheath, first lateral then posteromedial to the external carotid, to the external opening of the carotid canal.

details.label: Branches
details.value: None in the neck.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: No cervical structures; all flow continues to the brain and orbit.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Internal jugular vein lateral, vagus nerve posterolateral, sympathetic trunk behind; crossed laterally by the hypoglossal nerve, occipital artery and posterior belly of digastric; styloid muscles and glossopharyngeal nerve pass between it and the external carotid.

cards.pearl: Atherosclerotic plaque at its origin is the classic source of emboli causing amaurosis fugax and anterior-circulation TIA or stroke; cervical dissection gives neck pain with a painful Horner syndrome.

cards.name: Petrous part of internal carotid artery
cards.function: Second part of the internal carotid, running through the carotid canal of the temporal bone.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the cervical part at the external opening of the carotid canal.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends, then bends anteromedially in the carotid canal in front of the tympanic cavity and cochlea, and passes above the cartilage filling the foramen lacerum to enter the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Caroticotympanic artery (to the tympanic cavity) and artery of the pterygoid canal (an internal-to-external carotid anastomosis).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Tympanic cavity; anastomotic supply toward the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Surrounded by the internal carotid sympathetic plexus and a venous plexus; the auditory tube and tensor tympani lie anterolateral, the trigeminal ganglion above its roof.

cards.pearl: A thin or dehiscent bony wall lets carotid pulsation be heard as pulsatile tinnitus and puts the artery at risk in middle-ear surgery.

cards.name: Cavernous part of internal carotid artery
cards.function: Third part of the internal carotid, forming the S-shaped carotid siphon inside the cavernous sinus and supplying the pituitary, nearby dura and cranial nerves.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the petrous part above the foramen lacerum.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward in the carotid sulcus on the side of the sphenoid body within the cavernous sinus, then turns up medial to the anterior clinoid process to pierce the dural roof.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Meningohypophyseal trunk (tentorial branch, dorsal meningeal artery, inferior hypophyseal artery); artery to the inferior cavernous sinus (inferolateral trunk) with a branch to the superior orbital fissure; recurrent artery of foramen lacerum; branches to foramen rotundum, foramen ovale and foramen spinosum; meningeal and cavernous branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Neurohypophysis, dura of the tentorium and clivus, trigeminal ganglion and the nerves in the cavernous sinus wall.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Abducens nerve lies directly lateral to it inside the sinus; oculomotor, trochlear, ophthalmic and maxillary nerves lie in the lateral wall; the hypophysis is medial.

cards.pearl: Rupture here produces a carotid-cavernous fistula with pulsating exophthalmos, chemosis, an orbital bruit and ophthalmoplegia.

cards.name: Cerebral part of internal carotid artery
cards.function: Terminal, intradural part of the internal carotid that gives the ophthalmic artery and the anterior circulation of the brain.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the cavernous part after it pierces the dura medial to the anterior clinoid process.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs back and up below the optic nerve, lateral to the optic chiasm, to the anterior perforated substance where it divides.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Ophthalmic artery, superior hypophyseal arteries, posterior communicating artery, anterior choroidal artery; terminal anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Orbit and retina, pituitary stalk and adenohypophysis (via the portal system), optic chiasm and tract, internal capsule, and most of the cerebral hemisphere.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic nerve above and medial, oculomotor nerve lateral, anterior clinoid process lateral.

cards.pearl: An aneurysm at the origin of the posterior communicating artery compresses the oculomotor nerve, giving a painful third-nerve palsy with a dilated pupil.

cards.name: Mandibular (first) part of maxillary artery
cards.function: First part of the maxillary artery, whose branches all enter bone to supply the ear, the dura and the mandibular teeth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Larger terminal branch of the external carotid in the parotid gland behind the neck of the mandible.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs horizontally forward between the neck of the mandible and the sphenomandibular ligament, along the lower border of lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Deep auricular artery, anterior tympanic artery, middle meningeal artery, accessory meningeal artery, inferior alveolar artery (with its mylohyoid branch).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: External acoustic meatus and tympanic membrane, TMJ, dura and calvaria, mandible, lower teeth and chin.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve lies above; its two roots encircle the middle meningeal artery; maxillary veins accompany it.

cards.pearl: Every branch of this part passes through a foramen or canal, a useful rule for recalling them.

cards.name: Pterygoid (second) part of maxillary artery
cards.function: Second part of the maxillary artery, whose branches are all muscular and supply the muscles of mastication and the buccinator region.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the mandibular part at the lower border of lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs obliquely forward and up, superficial or deep to the lower head of lateral pterygoid, toward the pterygomaxillary fissure.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior and posterior deep temporal arteries, masseteric artery, medial and lateral pterygoid arteries, buccal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Temporalis, masseter, medial and lateral pterygoids, buccinator and cheek.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies within the pterygoid venous plexus; the buccal, lingual and inferior alveolar nerves are close to it.

cards.pearl: Bleeding from this part and the surrounding pterygoid plexus causes the hematoma that can follow a posterior superior alveolar nerve block.

cards.name: Pterygopalatine (third) part of maxillary artery
cards.function: Third part of the maxillary artery, distributing with the branches of the maxillary nerve to the nasal cavity, palate, upper teeth and face.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the pterygoid part as it passes between the two heads of lateral pterygoid.

details.label: Course
details.value: Enters the pterygopalatine fossa through the pterygomaxillary fissure and breaks up in front of the pterygopalatine ganglion.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Posterior superior alveolar artery, infraorbital artery (with middle and anterior superior alveolar arteries), descending palatine artery (greater and lesser palatine arteries), artery of the pterygoid canal, pharyngeal artery, sphenopalatine artery (terminal).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Maxillary teeth and sinus, lower eyelid and cheek, hard and soft palate, nasopharynx, nasal septum and lateral nasal wall.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies anterior to the pterygopalatine ganglion and the maxillary nerve in the fossa.

cards.pearl: Its sphenopalatine terminal branch is the vessel clipped or embolized for refractory posterior epistaxis.

cards.name: First part of subclavian artery
cards.function: Segment of the subclavian medial to the anterior scalene that gives the vertebral, internal thoracic and thyrocervical vessels.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Right: brachiocephalic trunk behind the sternoclavicular joint. Left: aortic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Arches up and laterally over the cervical pleura to the medial border of the anterior scalene.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Vertebral artery, internal thoracic artery, thyrocervical trunk (inferior thyroid, transverse cervical, suprascapular arteries).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Brain stem and cerebellum, anterior chest wall, thyroid gland, root of the neck and scapular region.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crossed anteriorly by the vagus and phrenic nerves and the internal jugular and vertebral veins; the ansa subclavia loops around it; the right recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks beneath it; the thoracic duct crosses the left one.

cards.pearl: Stenosis proximal to the vertebral origin causes subclavian steal: arm exercise reverses vertebral flow and produces vertebrobasilar symptoms with a lower blood pressure in that arm.

cards.name: Second part of subclavian artery
cards.function: Short highest segment of the subclavian lying behind the anterior scalene, giving the costocervical trunk.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the first part at the medial border of the anterior scalene.

details.label: Course
details.value: Forms the summit of the arch behind the anterior scalene, on the cervical pleura and suprapleural membrane.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Costocervical trunk (deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries).

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Deep muscles of the back of the neck and the first two intercostal spaces.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior scalene in front separates it from the subclavian vein and phrenic nerve; middle scalene and the lower trunk of the brachial plexus lie behind.

cards.name: Third part of subclavian artery
cards.function: Most superficial segment of the subclavian, crossing the first rib in the posterior triangle to become the axillary artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the second part at the lateral border of the anterior scalene.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs down and laterally across the posterior triangle and the upper surface of the first rib to its outer border.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Dorsal scapular artery when it is not the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery; often no branch.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Rhomboids and levator scapulae through the dorsal scapular artery; continues as the upper limb supply.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trunks of the brachial plexus lie above and behind, the lower trunk directly behind on the first rib; subclavian vein in front and below; crossed by the suprascapular vessels.

cards.pearl: Its pulse is felt, and it can be compressed against the first rib, in the angle between the clavicle and the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid; a cervical rib or tight scalene interval compresses it here in thoracic outlet syndrome.

cards.name: Prevertebral part of vertebral artery (V1)
cards.function: First part of the vertebral artery, from its subclavian origin to the transverse foramen of C6.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterosuperior aspect of the first part of the subclavian artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the angle between longus colli and the anterior scalene to enter the transverse foramen of C6.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Usually none.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: No territory of its own; carries flow toward the hindbrain.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Behind the common carotid artery and vertebral vein; crossed by the inferior thyroid artery (and the thoracic duct on the left); the cervicothoracic (stellate) ganglion lies behind it.

cards.pearl: Its origin is the commonest site of vertebral atherosclerosis.

cards.name: Cervical part of vertebral artery (V2)
cards.function: Second part of the vertebral artery, ascending through the cervical transverse foramina and reinforcing the supply of the cervical cord.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the prevertebral part at the transverse foramen of C6.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends through the transverse foramina of C6 to C1, in front of the anterior rami of the cervical nerves, with the vertebral venous plexus and sympathetic vertebral plexus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Segmental medullary (spinal) branches through the intervertebral foramina; muscular branches to the deep neck muscles.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Cervical spinal cord and meninges, vertebrae and deep cervical muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Uncovertebral joints lie medial; the C7 transverse foramen carries vertebral veins but usually not the artery.

cards.pearl: Uncovertebral osteophytes or neck rotation can compress the artery within the transverse foramina, causing vertebrobasilar insufficiency.

cards.name: Atlantic part of vertebral artery (V3, horizontal segment)
cards.function: Third part of the vertebral artery, curving behind the lateral mass of the atlas in the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the cervical part as it leaves the transverse foramen of the atlas.

details.label: Course
details.value: Winds posteromedially in the groove for the vertebral artery on the posterior arch of the atlas, then pierces the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane and dura.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Muscular branches to the suboccipital muscles, anastomosing with the descending branch of the occipital artery and the deep cervical artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Suboccipital muscles.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the floor of the suboccipital triangle with the suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1) between it and the posterior arch of the atlas.

cards.pearl: This mobile loop is the usual site of vertebral artery dissection after sudden neck rotation or manipulation, a cause of posterior-circulation stroke in young adults.

cards.name: Intracranial part of vertebral artery (V4)
cards.function: Fourth, intradural part of the vertebral artery, supplying the medulla, upper cord and inferior cerebellum before forming the basilar artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the atlantic part after it pierces the dura.

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the foramen magnum and runs up and medially in front of the medulla to the lower border of the pons, where it joins its fellow.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior and posterior meningeal branches, posterior spinal artery, posterior inferior cerebellar artery, anterior spinal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medulla, upper cervical cord, inferior cerebellum and dura of the posterior cranial fossa.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Rootlets of the hypoglossal nerve lie behind it; the first denticulate ligament and the spinal accessory root are posterior.

cards.pearl: Occlusion of this part, more often than of PICA itself, produces the lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.

cards.name: Aortic arch
cards.function: Arch of the aorta in the superior mediastinum, giving the three great vessels that supply the head, neck and upper limbs.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Branches from right to left: brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery. The aorta itself is labelled as ascending aorta, arch and descending aorta.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Continuation of the ascending aorta behind the right second sternocostal joint.

details.label: Course
details.value: Arches up, back and to the left over the root of the left lung, in front of and then to the left of the trachea, to the left side of T4.

details.label: Branches
details.value: In order: brachiocephalic trunk (to right common carotid and right subclavian), left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery; occasionally a thyroid ima artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Head, neck and both upper limbs through its three branches.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Left brachiocephalic vein crosses in front of its branches; left vagus and phrenic nerves cross its left side; the left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under it beside the ligamentum arteriosum.

cards.pearl: An arch aneurysm can stretch the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and present with hoarseness.

cards.name: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery
cards.function: Anterior terminal branch of the superficial temporal artery, supplying the temple and lateral forehead.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the superficial temporal artery on the temporal fascia about 2-3 cm above the zygomatic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs tortuously forward and up across the temple toward the forehead in the superficial fascia.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cutaneous and muscular twigs; anastomoses with the supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries and with its fellow.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin, frontalis and pericranium of the lateral forehead and anterior temple.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs with the temporal branches of the facial nerve and branches of the auriculotemporal nerve; the anastomosis with the supraorbital artery links external and internal carotid territories.

cards.pearl: This is the visible, tortuous temple vessel that is tender and nodular in giant cell arteritis and is the usual site of temporal artery biopsy.

cards.name: Parietal branch of superficial temporal artery
cards.function: Posterior terminal branch of the superficial temporal artery, supplying the parietal scalp.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the superficial temporal artery above the zygomatic arch.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends and curves backward over the temporal fascia and the side of the head.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cutaneous twigs; anastomoses with its fellow across the vertex and with the posterior auricular and occipital arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin and aponeurosis of the temporal and parietal scalp.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the dense connective tissue layer of the scalp with the auriculotemporal nerve.

cards.pearl: Scalp arteries are held open by the dense connective tissue layer and anastomose freely, so scalp lacerations bleed briskly from both cut ends.

cards.name: Frontal (anterior) branch of middle meningeal artery
cards.function: Larger anterior division of the middle meningeal artery, supplying the anterior dura and inner table of the skull.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the middle meningeal artery on the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Crosses the greater wing of the sphenoid, grooving or tunnelling the bone deep to the pterion, then ascends toward the vertex over the frontal and anterior parietal regions.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the dura, diploe and inner table; orbital (anastomotic) branch joining the recurrent meningeal branch of the lacrimal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dura and calvaria of the anterior and middle cranial fossae and frontoparietal convexity.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the dura and the bone immediately deep to the pterion, overlying the precentral region of the brain.

cards.pearl: A fracture through the pterion tears this branch, producing an epidural hematoma with a lucid interval and a biconvex collection on CT.

cards.name: Parietal (posterior) branch of middle meningeal artery
cards.function: Posterior division of the middle meningeal artery, supplying the posterior dura and calvaria.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Division of the middle meningeal artery on the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

details.label: Course
details.value: Curves backward over the squamous part of the temporal bone and the parietal bone toward the lambda.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the dura, diploe and inner table; anastomoses with the mastoid branch of the occipital artery and its fellow.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Dura and calvaria of the posterior parietal and occipital convexity.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs extradurally in grooves on the squamous temporal and parietal bones.

cards.name: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
cards.function: Branches of the sphenopalatine artery that supply most of the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Sphenopalatine artery as it enters the nasal cavity through the sphenopalatine foramen.

details.label: Course
details.value: Run forward over the middle and inferior nasal conchae and their meatuses.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the conchae and meatuses and to the maxillary, ethmoidal and sphenoidal sinuses; anastomose with the anterior lateral nasal branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery and the lateral nasal branch of the facial artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Mucosa of the lateral nasal wall, conchae and paranasal sinuses.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompany the posterior superior lateral nasal nerves from the pterygopalatine ganglion.

cards.pearl: They are the usual source of posterior epistaxis, controlled by endoscopic sphenopalatine artery ligation behind the middle concha.

cards.name: Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
cards.function: Terminal branches of the sphenopalatine artery that supply the nasal septum and join the anterior septal anastomosis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Sphenopalatine artery at the sphenopalatine foramen.

details.label: Course
details.value: Cross the roof of the nasal cavity on the anterior face of the sphenoid body to the septum, then run down and forward in a groove on the vomer to the incisive canal.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Septal twigs; anastomose with the greater palatine artery in the incisive canal, the septal branch of the superior labial artery and the anterior ethmoidal artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior and inferior nasal septum; contribute to Kiesselbach plexus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Run with the nasopalatine nerve.

cards.name: Medial and lateral palpebral arteries (palpebral arterial arches)
cards.function: Arteries of the eyelids, forming superior and inferior arterial arches between the ophthalmic and lacrimal arteries.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior medial palpebral artery and inferior medial palpebral artery (from ophthalmic); superior lateral palpebral artery and inferior lateral palpebral artery (from lacrimal); joined as the superior and inferior palpebral arterial arches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial palpebral arteries (superior and inferior) from the ophthalmic artery below the trochlea; lateral palpebral arteries (superior and inferior) from the lacrimal artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Enter the lids at the medial and lateral angles and run toward each other between orbicularis oculi and the tarsal plates.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Superior and inferior palpebral arterial arches; twigs to conjunctiva and nasolacrimal duct; anastomoses with the angular, transverse facial, zygomatico-orbital and supraorbital arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Eyelids, tarsal glands, palpebral conjunctiva.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie on the anterior surface of the tarsi deep to orbicularis oculi.

cards.pearl: The lids are a meeting point of external and internal carotid territories, so they heal quickly and bleed freely.

cards.name: Long medial striate artery (recurrent artery of Heubner)
cards.function: Largest perforating branch of the anterior cerebral artery, supplying the anterior deep structures of the hemisphere.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery at or just beyond the anterior communicating artery (proximal A2 or distal A1).

details.label: Course
details.value: Doubles back laterally along the A1 segment to enter the anterior perforated substance.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating branches only.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Head of the caudate nucleus, anterior putamen and anterior limb of the internal capsule.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Runs above the A1 segment and optic nerve, close to the anterior communicating artery.

cards.pearl: Occlusion, for example during clipping of an anterior communicating aneurysm, gives contralateral face and arm weakness with dysarthria.

cards.name: Medial frontobasal (medial orbitofrontal) artery
cards.function: First cortical branch of the anterior cerebral artery, supplying the medial orbital surface of the frontal lobe.

details.label: Origin
details.value: A2 segment of the anterior cerebral artery just beyond the anterior communicating artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward along the gyrus rectus and medial orbital surface.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Gyrus rectus, medial orbital gyri, olfactory bulb and tract.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies on the floor of the anterior cranial fossa beside the olfactory tract.

cards.name: Callosomarginal artery
cards.function: Major branch of the anterior cerebral artery running in the cingulate sulcus to the medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior medial frontal branch, intermediate medial frontal branch, posterior medial frontal branch, cingular branches, paracentral artery.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (A2) near the genu of the corpus callosum.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward in the cingulate sulcus above the cingulate gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior, intermediate and posterior medial frontal branches, cingular branches, paracentral artery.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial surface of the superior frontal gyrus, cingulate gyrus, and the paracentral lobule (leg and foot motor and sensory cortex).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies beside the falx cerebri, above the pericallosal artery.

cards.pearl: Infarction of its paracentral territory causes contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss with urinary incontinence; subfalcine herniation can compress it against the falx.

cards.name: Pericallosal artery
cards.function: Continuation of the anterior cerebral artery over the corpus callosum to the medial parietal lobe.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery beyond the origin of the callosomarginal artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward in the callosal sulcus on the body of the corpus callosum toward the splenium.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Branches to the corpus callosum, precuneal artery, terminal cortical branches reaching the superolateral surface.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Corpus callosum (genu and body), cingulate gyrus, precuneus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies under the free edge of the falx cerebri; anastomoses with the dorsal branch to corpus callosum of the posterior cerebral artery at the splenium.

cards.name: Anterolateral central (lenticulostriate) arteries
cards.function: Small end-arteries from the stem of the middle cerebral artery that supply the basal ganglia and internal capsule.

details.label: Origin
details.value: M1 segment of the middle cerebral artery (proximal medial and distal lateral groups).

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascend at right angles through the anterior perforated substance into the hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating end-arteries without significant anastomoses.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Putamen, globus pallidus, body of the caudate nucleus and the genu and posterior limb of the internal capsule.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Enter the brain lateral to the optic tract; the long medial striate artery enters medial to them.

cards.pearl: Hypertensive lipohyalinosis and Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms of these vessels cause lacunar infarcts (pure motor stroke) and putaminal hemorrhage.

cards.name: Lateral frontobasal (lateral orbitofrontal) artery
cards.function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery to the lateral orbital surface and inferior frontal gyrus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and up over the lateral orbital surface of the frontal lobe.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lateral orbital gyri and the orbital part of the inferior frontal gyrus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerges from the anterior ramus of the lateral sulcus.

cards.name: Prefrontal artery
cards.function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery to the lateral prefrontal cortex.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Fans upward over the triangular and opercular parts of the inferior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Inferior and middle frontal gyri, including Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere and the frontal eye field.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerges from the lateral sulcus over the frontal operculum.

cards.pearl: Occlusion in the dominant hemisphere produces Broca (nonfluent) aphasia; involvement of the frontal eye field deviates the eyes toward the lesion.

cards.name: Artery of precentral sulcus
cards.function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the precentral sulcus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the precentral sulcus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs to the adjoining gyri.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Posterior parts of the middle and inferior frontal gyri and the lower precentral gyrus (premotor cortex and face and arm motor cortex).

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in front of the artery of the central sulcus.

cards.name: Artery of central sulcus
cards.function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the central sulcus to the primary motor and sensory cortex.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (superior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the central sulcus toward the superior margin of the hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs to the precentral and postcentral gyri.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Precentral and postcentral gyri for the face and upper limb.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the arteries of the precentral and postcentral sulci; its territory meets the anterior cerebral territory near the superior margin.

cards.pearl: Occlusion causes contralateral weakness and sensory loss of the face and arm with relative sparing of the leg.

cards.name: Artery of postcentral sulcus (anterior parietal artery)
cards.function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery running in the postcentral sulcus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the postcentral sulcus and then back along the intraparietal sulcus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Postcentral gyrus (face and arm somatosensory cortex) and anterior part of the parietal lobules.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies behind the artery of the central sulcus.

cards.name: Posterior parietal artery
cards.function: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery to the posterior parietal lobe.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (inferior or superior division) at the posterior end of the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Emerges from the posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus and runs up and back over the supramarginal gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Supramarginal gyrus and inferior and superior parietal lobules.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the artery of the postcentral sulcus and the artery to the angular gyrus.

cards.pearl: Infarction of the non-dominant parietal lobe causes contralateral hemispatial neglect.

cards.name: Artery to angular gyrus
cards.function: Terminal cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery, supplying the angular gyrus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal part of the middle cerebral artery at the posterior end of the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs back over the superior temporal gyrus to the angular gyrus.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Angular gyrus and adjoining parts of the supramarginal gyrus and lateral occipital cortex.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its territory borders the posterior cerebral territory in the posterior watershed zone.

cards.pearl: Dominant angular gyrus infarction gives Gerstmann syndrome: agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia and left-right disorientation.

cards.name: Temporal branches of middle cerebral artery (anterior, middle and posterior)
cards.function: Cortical branches of the inferior division of the middle cerebral artery, supplying the lateral temporal lobe.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Polar temporal artery (temporal pole), anterior temporal artery, middle temporal artery, posterior temporal artery (continuing as the temporo-occipital branch).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (inferior division) in the lateral sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Descend out of the lateral sulcus over the superior and middle temporal gyri; the posterior branch continues toward the occipital lobe as the temporo-occipital branch.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Cortical twigs.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Temporal pole and the superior and middle temporal gyri, including the primary auditory cortex and Wernicke's area in the dominant hemisphere.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerge under the temporal operculum.

cards.pearl: Dominant inferior-division occlusion causes Wernicke (fluent) aphasia, often with a contralateral superior quadrantanopia.

cards.name: Thalamoperforating and thalamogeniculate arteries
cards.function: Perforating branches of the posterior cerebral artery that supply the thalamus and upper midbrain.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Thalamoperforating arteries (from P1, through the posterior perforated substance); thalamogeniculate arteries (from P2, to the posterolateral thalamus and geniculate bodies).

details.label: Origin
details.value: Thalamoperforating (posteromedial central) arteries from the P1 segment; thalamogeniculate arteries from the P2 segment.

details.label: Course
details.value: Thalamoperforating arteries enter the posterior perforated substance in the interpeduncular fossa; thalamogeniculate arteries enter the brain around the geniculate bodies.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating end-arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Medial and anterior thalamus, subthalamus and paramedian midbrain (thalamoperforating); ventral posterior and lateral thalamus and geniculate bodies (thalamogeniculate).

details.label: Relations
details.value: The oculomotor nerve emerges among the thalamoperforating vessels in the interpeduncular fossa.

cards.pearl: Thalamogeniculate infarction causes contralateral hemisensory loss followed by thalamic pain (Dejerine-Roussy syndrome).

cards.name: Posterior medial and posterior lateral choroidal arteries
cards.function: Branches of the posterior cerebral artery supplying the choroid plexuses of the third and lateral ventricles.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Posterior medial choroidal artery (to choroid plexus of the 3rd ventricle); posterior lateral choroidal artery (to choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle).

details.label: Origin
details.value: P2 segment of the posterior cerebral artery.

details.label: Course
details.value: Posterior medial choroidal artery curves around the midbrain to the roof of the third ventricle; posterior lateral choroidal artery passes over the pulvinar through the choroidal fissure into the lateral ventricle.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Twigs to the tectum, pineal region, pulvinar, lateral geniculate body and fornix.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Choroid plexus of the third ventricle (medial); choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle, pulvinar and lateral geniculate body (lateral).

details.label: Relations
details.value: The posterior lateral choroidal artery anastomoses with the anterior choroidal artery in the choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle.

cards.name: Medial occipital artery (parieto-occipital and calcarine branches)
cards.function: Medial terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery, supplying the primary visual cortex.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Dorsal branch to corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal artery), parieto-occipital branch (in the parieto-occipital sulcus), calcarine branch (in the calcarine sulcus), occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery behind the midbrain.

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward on the medial surface of the occipital lobe toward the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Dorsal branch to corpus callosum (posterior pericallosal artery), parieto-occipital branch, calcarine branch, occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Splenium of the corpus callosum, cuneus, precuneus, lingual gyrus and the primary visual cortex on the banks of the calcarine sulcus.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies under the splenium beside the great cerebral vein and the free edge of the tentorium.

cards.pearl: Occlusion gives contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing, because the occipital pole also receives middle cerebral collaterals.

cards.name: Temporal branches of posterior cerebral artery (lateral occipital artery)
cards.function: Lateral terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery, supplying the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior temporal artery, posterior temporal artery, occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Terminal division of the posterior cerebral artery behind the midbrain.

details.label: Course
details.value: Run laterally and backward across the parahippocampal and occipitotemporal gyri on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Anterior temporal artery, posterior temporal artery, occipitotemporal branches.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Uncus, hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus, and the medial and lateral occipitotemporal (fusiform) gyri.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie on the tentorium cerebelli; the artery is compressed against the tentorial edge in uncal herniation.

cards.pearl: Bilateral or dominant inferior temporal infarction causes memory impairment, and fusiform involvement causes prosopagnosia.

cards.name: Pontine arteries
cards.function: Numerous small branches of the basilar artery that supply the pons.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Medial (paramedian) pontine branches; lateral (short and long circumferential) pontine branches.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Both sides of the basilar artery along the basilar sulcus.

details.label: Course
details.value: Paramedian (medial) branches enter the pons beside the midline; short and long circumferential (lateral) branches wind around its sides.

details.label: Branches
details.value: Perforating end-arteries.

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts, pontine nuclei, medial lemniscus, abducens nucleus and fibres, and the lateral pontine tegmentum.

details.label: Relations
details.value: The abducens nerve emerges at the lower border of the pons between them.

cards.pearl: Bilateral paramedian pontine infarction from basilar thrombosis causes locked-in syndrome; lacunar occlusion of one perforator causes pure motor hemiparesis or ataxic hemiparesis.
